key_insight: MAGNet is a Transformer-style graph neural network that adaptively fuses multi-scale structural and functional brain connectomes, learning interpretable structure–function interactions that improve cognitive prediction and insight.
problem_solved: Jointly modeling complementary but mismatched structural (morphology) and functional (connectivity) brain networks is hard; MAGNet addresses scale differences and rigid fusion schemes by learning adaptive, multi-scale interactions between modalities.
method: Multi-scale adaptive graph attention: a Transformer-style GNN that builds graphs at multiple spatial scales and learns attention weights to modulate inter- and intra-scale edges.

Multimodal integration: uses source-based morphometry (sMRI) morphological features as node attributes together with functional connectivity (fMRI) edges, fusing them end-to-end to capture cross-modal relationships.
Task-driven training & interpretability: trained for cognitive prediction with attention maps that highlight region-level structure–function contributions for downstream analysis.
impact: MAGNet provides a principled, interpretable approach for multimodal graph representation learning in neuroscience; AI/ML practitioners can adapt its multi-scale adaptive attention to other domains where heterogeneous graphs and cross-modal interactions matter.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: multi-scale graph layers with Transformer-style attention blocks showing how structural and functional streams are fused.
Brain overlay: anatomical surface with structural morphology nodes and functional connectivity edges, colored by learned attention strengths.
Attention heatmaps: region-by-region attention matrices at different scales to illustrate interpretability and key structure–function links.
Performance chart: bar/line plot comparing MAGNet vs. baseline models on cognitive prediction metrics (e.g., accuracy/R^2) to show empirical gains.
paper_title: Learning Structural-Functional Brain Representations through Multi-Scale Adaptive Graph Attention for Cognitive Insight
paper_authors: Badhan Mazumder, Sir-Lord Wiafe, Aline Kotoski, Vince D. Calhoun, Dong Hye Ye
